sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In 1980, a bomb exploded at the central train station in Bologna, Italy.
sentences.zh: 1980年，意大利博洛尼亚的中央火车站发生了一起爆炸。

sentences.en: 85 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 85人遇难。

sentences.en: Hundreds were injured.
sentences.zh: 数百人受伤。

sentences.en: In the wake of the attack, which was later blamed on an Italian terrorist organization,
sentences.zh: 在那次袭击发生后不久——后来这起袭击被归咎于一个意大利恐怖组织，

sentences.en: a large clock on the outside of the train station stopped working.
sentences.zh: 火车站外侧的一座大钟停止了运转。

sentences.en: The clock, frozen at 10.25, became a symbol of the attack.
sentences.zh: 这座定格在10点25分的时钟，成了袭击的象征。

sentences.en: The picture of the clock was plastered all over posters and banners
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，

sentences.en: during commemorations of the event for years afterwards.
sentences.zh: 每当举行事件纪念活动时，时钟的照片都会被贴满海报和横幅。

sentences.en: The clock was quickly repaired.
sentences.zh: 这座时钟很快就被修好了。

sentences.en: But in 1996, 16 years after the bombing,
sentences.zh: 但在1996年，即爆炸案发生的16年后，

sentences.en: city officials permanently stopped the clock at 10.25 in remembrance of the tragedy.
sentences.zh: 城市官员将时钟永久定格在10点25分，以此缅怀这场悲剧。

sentences.en: In so doing, they unwittingly set up a psychological experiment.
sentences.zh: 在这样做的同时，他们无意中设置了一项心理学实验。

sentences.en: Decades later, when asked whether the clock had ever been fixed,
sentences.zh: 几十年后，当被问及这座时钟是否曾被修好过时，

sentences.en: the vast majority of city residents incorrectly reported that it had not.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数城市居民都错误地回答说没有。

sentences.en: That included 21 employees of the train station,
sentences.zh: 其中包括火车站的21名员工，

sentences.en: who presumably saw the clock on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 他们按理说应该经常看到这座时钟。

sentences.en: It's not difficult to understand how this error might have come about.
sentences.zh: 不难理解这种错误是如何产生的。

sentences.en: The stopped clock had become an integral element of the story of the bombing.
sentences.zh: 这座停止的时钟已经成了轰炸故事中不可或缺的一个元素。

sentences.en: People's recollections were shaped by the story as much as the facts.
sentences.zh: 人们的回忆不仅受事实影响，也同样被这个故事所塑造。

sentences.en: We see the same thing happening in settings large and small.
sentences.zh: 我们在大小不同的各种场景中都能看到同样的现象。

sentences.en: Two friends might disagree about an incident that took place
sentences.zh: 两个朋友可能会对过去一起在学校时发生的一起事件

sentences.en: when they were in school together, years before.
sentences.zh: 各执一词，尽管那是多年前的事了。

sentences.en: Managers and workers may remember different versions of the events that led to a strike,
sentences.zh: 管理者和工人们可能会对引发罢工的事件记得截然不同的版本，

sentences.en: with each group partial to the version that supports its point of view.
sentences.zh: 每个群体都偏向于支持自己观点的版本。

sentences.en: When countries go to war,
sentences.zh: 当国家陷入战争时，

sentences.en: millions of people may collectively remember one chronicle of historical wrongs,
sentences.zh: 数以百万计的人可能会集体铭记一段历史冤屈的叙事，

sentences.en: while millions of people on the other side of a border remember a completely different set of facts.
sentences.zh: 而国境线另一侧数以百万计的人则会记住一套完全不同的事实。

sentences.en: Many of us roll our eyes at people who misremember things to soothe their preferred narratives about the world.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人会对那些为了让自已对世界的偏爱叙事好受一些而记错事情的人翻白眼。

sentences.en: The one thing we all find hard to do?
sentences.zh: 而我们所有人都觉得最难做到的是什么？

sentences.en: Believe that our memories are just as fallible,
sentences.zh: 是相信我们的记忆同样不可靠，

sentences.en: and shaped by our own thoughts, beliefs, and stories.
sentences.zh: 并且是由我们自己的想法、信念和故事塑造的。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，

sentences.en: how preferences, loyalties, and the power of suggestion
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨偏好、忠诚以及暗示的力量

sentences.en: can shape what we remember and what we forget.
sentences.zh: 如何塑造我们的记忆与遗忘。

sentences.en: Long before Elizabeth Loftus became a psychologist and a researcher who studied memory,
sentences.zh: 早在伊丽莎白·洛夫图斯成为一名研究记忆的心理学家和研究人员之前，

sentences.en: long before she became one of the world's experts on the way we recollect childhood traumas,
sentences.zh: 早在她成为研究我们如何回忆童年创伤的世界顶尖专家之前，

sentences.en: she herself suffered three traumatic events as a child.
sentences.zh: 她自己在童年时期就遭遇过三次创伤性事件。

sentences.en: Each of them became, in their own way,
sentences.zh: 它们各自以独特的方式，

sentences.en: emblematic of her research into the slippery, fallible nature of memory.
sentences.zh: 成为了她对记忆那捉摸不定、不可靠本质进行研究的缩影。

sentences.en: My mother, I would say, developed depression when I was about 13 years old.
sentences.zh: 我可以说，自我大约13岁起，我母亲就患上了抑郁症。

sentences.en: And she went to Pennsylvania to get some treatment,
sentences.zh: 她去了宾夕法尼亚州接受一些治疗，

sentences.en: because that's where her brother lived, my Uncle Joe.
sentences.zh: 因为我舅舅乔在那儿住。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: And were you aware, as a 13-year-old, that your mom was unwell?
sentences.zh: 作为一名13岁的孩子，你当时知道你妈妈生病了吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes, I was definitely aware.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我绝对知道。

sentences.en: You know, even before she left to go to Pennsylvania for some treatment,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，甚至在她去宾夕法尼亚接受治疗之前，

sentences.en: my parents had tickets to different concerts or events,
sentences.zh: 我父母买好了不同音乐会或活动的门票，

sentences.en: and so my mother couldn't go to one of the events where they had tickets.
sentences.zh: 所以母亲无法去其中一场他们买过票的活动。

sentences.en: And so my father took me, I think it might have been a Gilbert and Sullivan play,
sentences.zh: 于是我父亲带我去了，我想那可能是一部吉尔伯特和沙利文的戏剧，

sentences.en: or it might have been, well, who, I can't remember exactly.
sentences.zh: 也可能是，嗯，具体是谁，我记不清了。

sentences.en: But I do remember driving back from the play to our house and stopping at a stoplight,
sentences.zh: 但我确实记得看完戏后开车回家的路上，在一个红绿灯处停下，

sentences.en: and some people were crossing the street.
sentences.zh: 有些人正在过马路。

sentences.en: And they were laughing and having a good time.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里说说笑笑，玩得很开心。

sentences.en: So it would have been after a play ends in Los Angeles, whatever time that would be.
sentences.zh: 所以那应该是在洛杉矶的一场戏结束之后，具体是几点钟就不知道了。

sentences.en: And they were having fun.
sentences.zh: 他们当时玩得很开心。

sentences.en: And my father said, see those people having fun.
sentences.zh: 我父亲说，看那些人玩得多开心。

sentences.en: And your mother can't have fun anymore.
sentences.zh: 而你母亲再也不能享受到这种快乐了。

sentences.en: So that's just one thing that sticks out in my memory now that you're asking.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你问起来，这只是我记忆中挥之不去的一件事。

sentences.en: So when she went to Pennsylvania, she went to her brother's home.
sentences.zh: 所以当她去宾夕法尼亚时，她去了她哥哥的家。

sentences.en: You said that she went there for treatment.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说她是去那里接受治疗的。

sentences.en: What happened there?
sentences.zh: 那里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Her older brother, you know, my Uncle Joe,
sentences.zh: 她的哥哥，你知道的，也就是我的舅舅乔，

sentences.en: wanted her to get this excellent treatment in a hospital in Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 想让她去匹兹堡的一家医院接受这种极好的治疗。

sentences.en: So he brought her, or he managed to get her to Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 于是他把她带了过来，或者说设法把她带到了宾夕法尼亚，

sentences.en: where he got her treatment in a nearby hospital.
sentences.zh: 在那里他在附近的一家医院给她安排了治疗。

sentences.en: And then she was released and ready to come home.
sentences.zh: 后来她出院了，准备回家。

sentences.en: So I went with my aunt by car to go pick her up and drive her back to California.
sentences.zh: 于是我和我阿姨开车去接她，开车把她带回加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: And she was staying at her brother's.
sentences.zh: 她当时住在她哥哥家里。

sentences.en: And when she was there, she ended up drowning in a swimming pool
sentences.zh: 就在她待在那里的时候，她最终在一个游泳池里溺水身亡了，

sentences.en: on my uncle's property in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 那个游泳池位于我舅舅在宾夕法尼亚的房产内。

sentences.en: So that was horrible.
sentences.zh: 所以那是极其可怕的。

sentences.en: How did that happen, Beth?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么发生的，贝丝？

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: We absolutely don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道。

sentences.en: But there was, you know, there were a lot of questions of,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，当时有很多疑问，

sentences.en: was it an accident?
sentences.zh: 是一场意外吗？

sentences.en: Was it a suicide?
sentences.zh: 是自杀吗？

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 到底是什么？

sentences.en: But it was never, ever decided.
sentences.zh: 但这件事从来没有、从来没有定论。

sentences.en: Nothing definitive.
sentences.zh: 没有什么确切的结果。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So you were actually there when this terrible thing happened, Beth?
sentences.zh: 所以这件可怕的事情发生时，你其实就在现场吗，贝丝？

sentences.en: I was, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在。

sentences.en: I was 14.
sentences.zh: 我当时14岁。

sentences.en: It was terrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: I mean, it was like the worst thing that ever happened to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像我经历过的最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Many years later, Beth found herself disagreeing with an uncle about what happened on that terrible day.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，贝丝发现自己和一位舅舅对那个可怕日子里发生的事情产生了分歧。

sentences.en: I went to a family event.
sentences.zh: 我去参加了一个家庭活动。

sentences.en: In fact, it was like a 90th birthday party of one of my uncles.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那就像是我的一位舅舅的90岁生日派对。

sentences.en: And while I was there, an uncle said to me, you know, back when your mother died, so that would have been, you know, decades earlier,
sentences.zh: 当我在那里时，一位舅舅对我说，你知道的，当年你母亲去世的时候，那大概是，你知道的，几十年前的事了，

sentences.en: you were the one who found your mother's body.
sentences.zh: 你是那个发现你母亲尸体的人。

sentences.en: And I said to my uncle, no, it wasn't me.
sentences.zh: 我对舅舅说，不，不是我。

sentences.en: It was her sister, my aunt who found the body.
sentences.zh: 是我姐姐，我的阿姨发现了尸体。

sentences.en: I'm not the one who found the body.
sentences.zh: 我不是那个发现尸体的人。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, you were.
sentences.zh: 哦，不对，就是你。

sentences.en: This relative was so absolutely positive.
sentences.zh: 这位亲戚是如此的绝对笃定。

sentences.en: And so I went home and I started thinking, did I find the body?
sentences.zh: 于是我回到家开始思考，难道真的是我发现了尸体吗？

sentences.en: And I started to try to remember what had happened on that day in 1959 when my mother drowned.
sentences.zh: 我开始试图回想1959年我母亲溺水的那天到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I did remember that when the 911, you know, emergency people came, the fireman ended up giving me oxygen.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得当911，也就是紧急救援人员到来时，消防员最后给我吸了氧。

sentences.en: And I thought maybe I was so upset I needed oxygen because I had found the body.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，也许我是因为太难过了才需要吸氧，因为我发现了尸体。

sentences.en: And I started working on this idea.
sentences.zh: 我开始顺着这个思路想下去。

sentences.en: And pretty soon I could see my mother drowned in the swimming pool with face down, with her arms out.
sentences.zh: 很快，我脑海中就能浮现出我母亲脸朝下、双臂伸开溺死在游泳池里的画面。

sentences.en: And I was visualizing it.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在脑海中将它可视化。

sentences.en: And then the relative called me and said, I'm calling to tell you I made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 然后那位亲戚打电话给我说，我打电话来是想告诉你我搞错了。

sentences.en: It wasn't you who found the body.
sentences.zh: 发现尸体的不是你。

sentences.en: Hey, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你说得对。

sentences.en: It was your aunt, her sister.
sentences.zh: 是你阿姨，她的姐姐。

sentences.en: And I was so amazed at the personal experience that I had just had.
sentences.zh: 我对刚刚经历的这段亲身经历感到无比震惊。

sentences.en: I was the subject in one of my own experiments.
sentences.zh: 我竟然成了自己实验中的被试。

sentences.en: This is what it's like for my subjects.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的被试们的感受。

sentences.en: I mean, why did, you know, why was my visualization with her face down, with her arms out?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么，你知道的，为什么我的视觉化影像是她脸朝下、双臂伸开的？

sentences.en: I mean, as opposed to on her back, you know, with no arms out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，而不是仰面朝天，你知道的，双臂没有伸开的那种？

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道。

sentences.en: Another traumatic event from Beth's childhood took place while she was in high school.
sentences.zh: 贝丝童年的另一个创伤性事件发生在她读高中时。

sentences.en: Her house was engulfed in a California wildfire that burned some 500 houses.
sentences.zh: 她的房子被加利福尼亚的一场野火吞噬了，那场大火烧毁了大约500栋房屋。

sentences.en: I was driving home from high school.
sentences.zh: 我当时正驾车从高中回家。

sentences.en: I was driving my brother, my younger brother, David.
sentences.zh: 我载着我的弟弟，我的小弟弟大卫。

sentences.en: And the streets were blocked off because of the fire.
sentences.zh: 由于火灾，街道都被封锁了。

sentences.en: But we knew secret ways to get past the roadblocks and get to the house and came upon the house burning down.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道绕过路障到达房子的秘密小路，结果发现房子正在燃烧。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: What was the reaction when you saw that?
sentences.zh: 当你看到那一幕时，你的反应是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, it must have been incredibly traumatic to see the...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看到那个场景一定极其痛苦……

sentences.en: No, I ran in the house to get some encyclopedias because I had homework to do.
sentences.zh: 不，我跑进屋去拿几本百科全书，因为我有作业要做。

sentences.en: And I got my encyclopedias and, you know, a few other items and went to a neighbor's house that was still intact and called my father at his office and said,
sentences.zh: 我拿了我的百科全书，还有，你知道的，一些其他物品，然后走到一处仍然完好的邻居家，用电话打给我办公室的父亲说，

sentences.en: the house isn't there anymore.
sentences.zh: 房子已经没了。

sentences.en: Beth has told the story of the fire many times.
sentences.zh: 贝丝曾多次讲述过这场火灾的故事。

sentences.en: Her memory of the incident is precise.
sentences.zh: 她对这起事件的记忆非常精确。

sentences.en: Unlike others who have been through similar events, she never exaggerates what happened.
sentences.zh: 与那些经历过类似事件的人不同，她从不夸大其词。

sentences.en: The reason?
sentences.zh: 原因是什么？

sentences.en: Any storytelling she might have been tempted to do has been constrained by a surprising source of documentary evidence.
sentences.zh: 她可能曾想做出的任何故事润色，都受到了一个令人惊讶的文献证据来源的限制。

sentences.en: I actually know something about this because there were photographers at the house from Life magazine.
sentences.zh: 其实我对这件事有所了解，因为当时《生活》杂志的摄影师就在现场。

sentences.en: So there was a very large spread about the fire itself and about our house in particular in Life magazine.
sentences.zh: 因此，《生活》杂志上用非常大的篇幅报道了这场大火本身，尤其是我们的房子。

sentences.en: If I could show you the Life magazine photos, you could see that, well, the house...
sentences.zh: 如果我能向你展示《生活》杂志的照片，你就会看到，嗯，房子……

sentences.en: It wasn't like it was engulfed in flames, but some people had already gone into the house to pull out some of our possessions and move them onto a concrete area.
sentences.zh: 它并不像被烈火吞噬的样子，而是已经有人走进屋去抢救我们的一些财产，把它们搬到了一个混凝土区域。

sentences.en: So it was possible for me to go in and get those encyclopedias.
sentences.zh: 所以我才有可能走进去拿到那些百科全书。

sentences.en: And it almost seems like what you're telling me is that you trust the pictures more than you trust your own memories.
sentences.zh: 听起来你对我说的话，似乎你比信任自己的记忆更信任那些照片。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: I can tell you because I've seen these pictures many times in Life magazine.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，因为我在《生活》杂志上看过这些照片很多次。

sentences.en: And it shows me standing in this concrete area looking at the burning house.
sentences.zh: 照片显示我站在这个混凝土区域，看着燃烧的房子。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: It shows me trying to carry some possessions away with my brother David.
sentences.zh: 照片显示我和弟弟大卫一起试图搬走一些财物。

sentences.en: It shows me on the phone at the neighbors calling my father.
sentences.zh: 照片显示我在邻居家的电话旁给父亲打电话。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The phone to my ear saying, Daddy, that house isn't there anymore.
sentences.zh: 电话贴在耳边说，爸爸，那栋房子已经不在了。

sentences.en: It, yeah, the pictures say it all.
sentences.zh: 这，是的，照片说明了一切。

sentences.en: To explain why Beth trusts the photos more than her memory, I need to wind the clock back and tell you about her strange journey through the labyrinths of human memory.
sentences.zh: 为了解释为什么贝丝比自己的记忆更信任照片，我需要把时间倒回，向你讲述她穿梭于人类记忆迷宫中的奇异旅程。

sentences.en: Also, we'll get to that third traumatic event from her childhood.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们还将谈到她童年的第三个创伤性事件。

sentences.en: Beth had never spoken in public about this incident until one day she blurted it out while serving as an expert witness in court.
sentences.zh: 贝丝过去从未在公开场合谈起过这件事，直到有一天她在法庭上作为专家证人作证时脱口而出。

sentences.en: I was testifying about the science of memory and the words just kind of came out.
sentences.zh: 我当时在作关于记忆科学的证词，那些话就那么自然而然地冒出来了。

sentences.en: It was the first time, certainly the first time I blurted it out publicly.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次，绝对是我第一次在公开场合说漏嘴。

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: In the early 1970s, Beth Loftus got a grant from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代初，贝丝·洛夫特斯获得了美国交通部的一笔资助

sentences.en: Department of Transportation to study how people remembered events involving auto crashes.
sentences.zh: 去研究人们是如何记住涉及车祸的事件的。

sentences.en: She was a newly minted psychologist, and she was interested both in the science of human memory and the implications of this science for the legal system.
sentences.zh: 她是一位初出茅庐的心理学家，既对人类记忆科学感兴趣，也对这门科学对法律体系的影响感兴趣。

sentences.en: She got her hands on police videos of traffic crashes and showed them to volunteers.
sentences.zh: 她弄到了交通车祸的警方录像，并把它们放给志愿者观看。

sentences.en: We would show people films of accidents and ask them about the speed of the vehicles.
sentences.zh: 我们会向人们展示事故的影像，并询问他们关于车辆速度的问题。

sentences.en: And different witnesses were questioned in different ways.
sentences.zh: 而且对不同的证人会用不同的方式进行盘问。

sentences.en: So some of our witnesses are asked how fast were the cars going when they hit each other.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的一些证人会被问到：当两辆车相撞时，它们的速度有多快？

sentences.en: Other witnesses are asked how fast were the cars going when they smashed into each other.
sentences.zh: 而其他证人则会被问到：当两辆车猛烈撞击时，它们的速度有多快？

sentences.en: And we might have used different verbs with other witnesses.
sentences.zh: 我们可能对其他证人使用了不同的动词。

sentences.en: But we found that people told us the cars were going faster if you use the word smashed than if you use the word hit.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现，如果你用“猛烈撞击（smashed）”这个词，人们告诉我们的车速会比你用“碰撞（hit）”这个词时更快。

sentences.en: So what we had shown at that point is just changing a word or two in your question can have an effect on the answer that somebody gave you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在当时所证明的是，仅仅改变你提问中的一两个词，就能对别人给你的回答产生影响。

sentences.en: Beth's study in 1974 revealed something subtle about human memory.
sentences.zh: 贝丝在1974年的研究揭示了人类记忆中微妙的一面。

sentences.en: When two cars were said to smash into each other, it painted a picture of the crash in volunteers' minds.
sentences.zh: 当听说两辆车“猛烈相撞”时，它在志愿者脑海中勾勒出了一幅事故的画面。

sentences.en: When Beth asked people about the crash, this image, the story it created in their minds, influenced what they remembered.
sentences.zh: 当贝丝向人们询问关于车祸的情况时，这种影像以及它在他们脑海中创造的故事，影响了他们的记忆。

sentences.en: Beth took the study a step further.
sentences.zh: 贝丝把这项研究推进了一步。

sentences.en: What we did then was we brought people back a week later and we said,
sentences.zh: 我们当时做的是，在一周后把人们请回来，然后我们说：

sentences.en: you know that accident we showed you last week, we have a few more questions for you.
sentences.zh: 你知道我们上周给你们看的那个事故吗？我们还有几个问题想问你。

sentences.en: Since broken glass is commensurate with a severe accident, one that occurs at higher speeds,
sentences.zh: 由于碎玻璃与严重事故相吻合，也就是那种在更高速度下发生的事故，

sentences.en: it's more likely that there was broken glass there and some people then think, yeah, they probably saw it.
sentences.zh: 那里有碎玻璃的可能性就更大，于是有些人就会想：是的，他们可能看到了。

sentences.en: So what this told us is that the way you word a question that you put to a witness can affect not only the immediate answer that you get,
sentences.zh: 所以这告诉我们，你向证人提问的措辞方式，不仅会影响你得到的即时回答，

sentences.en: but it can have a long-range effect.
sentences.zh: 还会产生长期影响。

sentences.en: It can affect the answer to some totally different question that you put to somebody, you know, often much, much later.
sentences.zh: 它可能会影响你向某人提出的某个完全不同的问题的答案，你知道的，通常是在很久很久之后。

sentences.en: In the second portion of the experiment, volunteers created visual details that never occurred.
sentences.zh: 在实验的第二部分，志愿者们凭空创造了从未发生过的视觉细节。

sentences.en: They thought they were remembering the facts, but without their awareness,
sentences.zh: 他们以为自己是在回忆事实，但在不知不觉中，

sentences.en: their minds had not only inferred the presence of broken glass at the scene of the crash,
sentences.zh: 他们的脑海中不仅推断出车祸现场有碎玻璃的存在，

sentences.en: but fabricated the sight of broken glass.
sentences.zh: 而且还凭空捏造出了看到碎玻璃的景象。

sentences.en: After the smash hit study, we did another study where what the subject sees is an accident unfold,
sentences.zh: 在“猛烈撞击”研究之后，我们做了另一项研究，被试看到的是一场事故的展开，

sentences.en: where let's say the car goes through an intersection with a yield sign.
sentences.zh: 比方说，汽车穿过一个有让行标志（yield sign）的十字路口。

sentences.en: After the accident is over, we asked a series of questions,
sentences.zh: 事故结束后，我们提出了一系列问题，

sentences.en: and one of them was designed to suggest some erroneous information.
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题旨在暗示一些错误的信息。

sentences.en: Did another car pass the red Datsun while it was there at the intersection with the stop sign?
sentences.zh: 当红色达特逊汽车停在那个有停车标志（stop sign）的十字路口时，有没有另一辆车从它旁边开过去？

sentences.en: This is a very clever question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常巧妙的问题。

sentences.en: You think I'm asking you about whether another car passed.
sentences.zh: 你以为我在问你是否真的有另一辆车开过去。

sentences.en: You're concentrating on that aspect of the question.
sentences.zh: 你的注意力集中在问题的那个方面。

sentences.en: You say, no, I didn't see another car pass.
sentences.zh: 你说：没有，我没看到有别的车开过去。

sentences.en: But I have cleverly slipped in the information that there was a stop sign there.
sentences.zh: 但我却巧妙地塞进了一条信息，即那里有一个停车标志。

sentences.en: You don't detect it.
sentences.zh: 你根本察觉不到。

sentences.en: And I think it invades people, almost like a Trojan horse,
sentences.zh: 我觉得它侵入了人们的脑海，几乎就像一只特洛伊木马，

sentences.en: because you don't even detect that it's coming.
sentences.zh: 因为你甚至察觉不到它的到来。

sentences.en: Later on, we can ask people, what kind of a traffic sign did you see there at the intersection?
sentences.zh: 随后，我们可以问人们：你在那里的十字路口看到了什么交通标志？

sentences.en: Was it a stop sign or a yield sign?
sentences.zh: 是停车标志还是让行标志？

sentences.en: And many people will pick the stop sign if they've succumbed to the suggestion in the leading question.
sentences.zh: 如果他们中了引导性问题的圈套，许多人会选择停车标志。

sentences.en: And there, I think what is going on is, when I ask you that leading question,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这里发生的情况是，当我向你提出那个引导性问题时：

sentences.en: did another car pass the red Datsun while it was there at the intersection with the stop sign,
sentences.zh: 当红色达特逊汽车停在那个有停车标志的十字路口时，有没有另一辆车从它旁边开过去？

sentences.en: you're trying to visualize what you saw,
sentences.zh: 你正在努力想象你所看到的情景，

sentences.en: and you just insert a well-known stop sign into your visualization.
sentences.zh: 而你只是在你的想象中插入了一个众所周知的停车标志。

sentences.en: And later on, when I say, what did you actually see there?
sentences.zh: 后来，当我说：你在那里究竟看到了什么？

sentences.en: You basically say stop sign, but you're seeing a stop sign that you yourself constructed.
sentences.zh: 你基本上会说停车标志，但你看到的其实是你自己构建出来的停车标志。

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, it's a more insidious form of the earlier study,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些方面，这是早期研究的一种更阴险的形式，

sentences.en: where you tell people the cars have smashed into each other,
sentences.zh: 在早期研究中，你告诉人们汽车“猛烈相撞”了，

sentences.en: and then you ask, did you see broken glass?
sentences.zh: 然后你问：你看到碎玻璃了吗？

sentences.en: There, people are saying, well, if the car smashed into each other,
sentences.zh: 在那里，人们会说：嗯，如果汽车猛烈相撞了，

sentences.en: there was probably broken glass.
sentences.zh: 那可能就会有碎玻璃。

sentences.en: And so, you know, perhaps it's an inference.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这或许是一种推论。

sentences.en: Perhaps they are recalling it.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是在回忆。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a mishmash between the two things.
sentences.zh: 也许这是两者之间的一种大杂烩。

sentences.en: But in this case, you're implanting a memory,
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，你是在植入一段记忆，

sentences.en: where you're suggesting that there's a stop sign instead of a yield sign,
sentences.zh: 即暗示有一个停车标志而不是让行标志，

sentences.en: and people just install their own stop sign and later remember seeing it.
sentences.zh: 而人们只是安插了自己的停车标志，并在后来记起曾看到过它。

sentences.en: I do feel like you're showing here the different ways in which memory can become contaminated.
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得你在这里展示了记忆被污染的不同方式。

sentences.en: One is just, I'm drawing an inference on my own and leading myself to a false conclusion.
sentences.zh: 一种只是我自己做出推论，并把自己引导到一个错误的结论上。

sentences.en: And in the next case, someone else is very subtly leading me to a wrong conclusion.
sentences.zh: 而在接下来的情况中，是别人在非常微妙地引导我走向错误的结论。

sentences.en: And both of those things can be going on at different times.
sentences.zh: 这两种情况都可能在不同的时间发生。

sentences.en: Or, to steal your wonderful term, it could be a mishmash.
sentences.zh: 或者，借用你那个美妙的词，这可能是一个大杂烩。

sentences.en: But we do know that people do draw inferences about what might have happened,
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，人们确实会对可能发生过的事情、

sentences.en: what could have happened, what probably happened.
sentences.zh: 可能发生的事情、大概发生过的事情做出推论。

sentences.en: And later on, those inferences kind of start to feel like memories.
sentences.zh: 而在后来，这些推论开始变得像是记忆一样。

sentences.en: And that's what you now remember.
sentences.zh: 而这也就是你现在所记住的东西。

sentences.en: Ancient philosophers like Plato and Aristotle compared memory to carvings on a wax tablet.
sentences.zh: 像柏拉图和亚里士多德这样的古代哲学家把记忆比作蜡板上的雕刻。

sentences.en: Aristotle proposed that the heart was the learning center of the body.
sentences.zh: 亚里士多德提出心脏是身体的学习中心。

sentences.en: Thus the phrase, learning by heart.
sentences.zh: 因此才有了“铭记于心（learning by heart）”这个短语。

sentences.en: In the 19th century, German scholar Hermann Ebbinghaus found that memories deteriorate over time
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，德国学者赫尔曼·艾宾浩斯发现记忆会随着时间而衰退，

sentences.en: and that constant repetition was key to preserving memory.
sentences.zh: 并且不断的重复是保持记忆的关键。

sentences.en: Sigmund Freud theorized that some memories were so unbearably painful
sentences.zh: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德建立了一种理论，认为有些记忆过于痛苦，以至于无法忍受，

sentences.en: that they were repressed into the subconscious mind.
sentences.zh: 以至于它们被压抑到了潜意识中。

sentences.en: All these were based on a model that human memory worked like a recording device.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是基于人类记忆像录音设备一样工作的模型。

sentences.en: Beth's study showed that memory was as much about inference, imagination, and suggestibility.
sentences.zh: 贝丝的研究表明，记忆同样关乎推断、想象和暗示性。

sentences.en: Rather than merely retrieving something that was recorded,
sentences.zh: 志愿者们并没有仅仅去检索被记录下来的东西，

sentences.en: volunteers were constructing events and passing off these inventions as recollections.
sentences.zh: 而是在构建事件，并把这些凭空捏造的东西当作回忆来蒙混过关。

sentences.en: The way I've often put it, memory doesn't work like a recording device.
sentences.zh: 正如我经常表达的那样，记忆的运作方式不像录音设备。

sentences.en: You don't just record the event and play it back later.
sentences.zh: 你不会只是记录下事件并在以后把它播放出来。

sentences.en: The process is much more complex.
sentences.zh: 这个过程要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And that's why we talk about the constructive nature of memory.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们要谈论记忆的建设性本质。

sentences.en: That when we're remembering things, we're frequently taking bits and pieces of experience,
sentences.zh: 当我们在回忆事情时，我们往往是在提取经验的零星片段，

sentences.en: sometimes things that happen at different times and places,
sentences.zh: 有时是发生在不同时间和地点的事件，

sentences.en: bringing it together to construct what feels to us like a memory.
sentences.zh: 并将它们组合在一起，构建出在我们看来像是记忆的东西。

sentences.en: And that's why we talk about the constructive or reconstructive nature of memory.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们谈论记忆的建设性或重建性本质。

sentences.en: Beth argues that the classic phrase,
sentences.zh: 贝丝认为，那个经典的短语——

sentences.en: we are the sum of our memories, needs an addendum.
sentences.zh: “我们是我们所有记忆的总和”——需要一个补充。

sentences.en: Our memories are not just the sum of what we've seen and heard,
sentences.zh: 我们的记忆不仅是我们所见所闻的总和，

sentences.en: but also what we think, what we believe, and what we want to believe.
sentences.zh: 也是我们的所思、所信以及我们想要相信的东西的总和。

sentences.en: She writes,
sentences.zh: 她写道：

sentences.en: We seem to reinvent our memories, and in doing so,
sentences.zh: 我们似乎在重塑我们的记忆，而在这样做的时候，

sentences.en: we become the person of our own imagination.
sentences.zh: 我们成为了我们自己的想象中的那个人。

sentences.en: Beth's studies raised questions about the reliability of eyewitness testimony,
sentences.zh: 贝丝的研究对目击者证词的可靠性提出了质疑，

sentences.en: a mainstay of the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 而目击者证词是刑事司法系统的顶梁柱。

sentences.en: Typically, this kind of evidence is treated as a slam dunk.
sentences.zh: 通常，这种证据被视为板上钉钉的事实。

sentences.en: But in one series of experiments that try to mimic what happens in such situations,
sentences.zh: 但在试图模仿此类情况下发生的事情的一系列实验中，

sentences.en: Beth suggested that our collective confidence in eyewitness testimony might be misplaced.
sentences.zh: 贝丝暗示，我们对目击证词的集体信任可能是错付了。

sentences.en: She staged a crime for volunteers.
sentences.zh: 她为志愿者策划了一场犯罪。

sentences.en: The crime was clearly committed by one person.
sentences.zh: 这起犯罪显然是由一个人所犯下的。

sentences.en: Now, you wait a few days,
sentences.zh: 现在，你等上几天，

sentences.en: and you ask your witnesses to look at six photos and try to pick the person who committed the bad act.
sentences.zh: 然后让你的证人看六张照片，并试图挑出实施不良行为的那个人。

sentences.en: The bad guy might be in that set of photos, or he might not be in the set of photos.
sentences.zh: 坏人可能在那组照片里，也可能不在那组照片里。

sentences.en: But many people will pick someone.
sentences.zh: 但许多人还是会选出一个人。

sentences.en: And then in a final test,
sentences.zh: 然后在最后的测试中，

sentences.en: there'll be a strong tendency to pick that same person again,
sentences.zh: 人们会有一种强烈的倾向，再次选择同一个人，

sentences.en: even if they're innocent,
sentences.zh: 即使他们是无辜的，

sentences.en: even if they were not the person who committed the bad act.
sentences.zh: 即使他们根本不是犯下恶行的人。

sentences.en: But he now looks pretty familiar because his photograph was seen,
sentences.zh: 但现在他看起来很面熟，因为人们见过他的照片，

sentences.en: not because he was seen in the event itself.
sentences.zh: 而不是因为在事件本身中见过他。

sentences.en: And that is exactly what happens when innocent people get misidentified
sentences.zh: 这正是无辜者被错认

sentences.en: and get convicted of crimes they didn't do.
sentences.zh: 并因他们未曾犯下的罪行而被定罪时所发生的情况。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So in this case here, it's another form of subtle memory manipulation, if you will,
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，如果你愿意的话，这是另一种微妙的记忆操纵形式，

sentences.en: because my own recollection of having seen someone makes that face more familiar to me.
sentences.zh: 因为我自己对见过某人的回忆，让那张脸对我来说更加熟悉了。

sentences.en: So the next time you show me that face,
sentences.zh: 所以下次你向我展示那张脸时，

sentences.en: I can't quite distinguish between a face that I myself picked out
sentences.zh: 我无法准确区分我亲手挑出的一张脸，

sentences.en: and a face that I might have actually seen at a crime scene, for example.
sentences.zh: 以及比如我可能在犯罪现场实际看到过的一张脸。

sentences.en: I get mixed up between those two things, and I conflate the two.
sentences.zh: 我在这两者之间糊涂了，并将它们混为一谈。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That kind of error can happen in other ways as well.
sentences.zh: 这种错误也可能以其他方式发生。

sentences.en: There's a famous example in one of the early books on eyewitness testimony,
sentences.zh: 在早期关于目击证词的一本著名书籍中有一个著名的例子，

sentences.en: written by a lawyer,
sentences.zh: 由一位律师撰写，

sentences.en: of a clerk in a train station who was robbed
sentences.zh: 讲的是火车站的一名职员遭到抢劫，

sentences.en: and goes to a lineup to try to identify the robber
sentences.zh: 他去列队辨认嫌疑人以试图认出劫匪，

sentences.en: and makes an identification.
sentences.zh: 并做出了辨认。

sentences.en: But he picked somebody who had purchased tickets from him
sentences.zh: 但他挑选的却是一个曾在过去几次向他买过票的人。

sentences.en: on a few prior occasions.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出这里发生了什么。

sentences.en: So you can see what's happening here.
sentences.zh: 职员去参加列队辨认。

sentences.en: The clerk goes to the lineup.
sentences.zh: 他在那队人中看到了且仅看到了一个熟悉的面孔。

sentences.en: He sees one and only one person familiar in that lineup.
sentences.zh: 他认定那就是劫匪。

sentences.en: He decides that that's the robber.
sentences.zh: 但这种熟悉感其实是由另一个原因、另一个理由造成的。

sentences.en: But that familiarity is really due to another cause, another reason.
sentences.zh: 这被称为无意识迁移。

sentences.en: And that's called an unconscious transference.
sentences.zh: 它是对在某种情况下见过的人的错误回忆，

sentences.en: It's the mistaken recollection of somebody who was seen in one situation,
sentences.zh: 而你却以为是在另一种情况下见到了他们。

sentences.en: and you think they were seen in a different situation.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，贝丝获得了参与一个实际法律案件的机会。

sentences.en: It was around this time that Beth got an opportunity to get involved
sentences.zh: 她当时在西雅图的华盛顿大学工作。

sentences.en: with an actual legal case.
sentences.zh: 那是一起谋杀案，被告是一名女性，

sentences.en: She was working at the University of Washington in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 而她的辩护理由是正当防卫。

sentences.en: It was a murder case where a woman was the defendant
sentences.zh: 那是一起女性作为被告的谋杀案

sentences.en: and her defense was self-defense.
sentences.zh: 而她的辩护理由是正当防卫。

sentences.en: Prosecution said it was murder.
sentences.zh: 检方称这是一起谋杀。

sentences.en: The defendant in the case was accused of killing a boyfriend
sentences.zh: 此案的被告被指控杀害了她的男友，

sentences.en: whom she charged with being abusive.

sentences.en: Maybe that could be a good thing.
sentences.zh: 或许这可以是一件好事。

sentences.en: But isn't your work also, in some ways, a call for intellectual and moral humility?
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，你的工作不也是一种对理智和道德谦逊的呼唤吗？

sentences.en: Because it tells us that perhaps we shouldn't be as confident in believing we know what we know,
sentences.zh: 因为它告诉我们，也许我们不该那么确信自己知道自己所知道的，

sentences.en: we remember what we remember, we think what we think.
sentences.zh: 我们记住自己所记住的，我们思考自己所思考的。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I believe that this is telling us that potentially there is a lot of fiction sprinkled
sentences.zh: 是的，我相信这在告诉我们，我们的头脑中可能潜藏着大量的虚构成分，

sentences.en: in there, in our minds, along with the facts.
sentences.zh: 与事实混杂在一起。

sentences.en: And this is maybe a truth that we should figure out how to respond to if it's going to be a problem,
sentences.zh: 如果这是一个问题，这也许是一个我们应该弄清楚如何去应对的真相，

sentences.en: or accept, and deal with, and live with, just like we might have blurry, bad vision,
sentences.zh: 或者去接受、应对并与之共存，就像我们可能会有模糊、糟糕的视力一样，

sentences.en: and we fix it with glasses or contact lenses.
sentences.zh: 然后我们用眼镜或隐形眼镜来矫正它。

sentences.en: And, you know, for me, as somebody who's been working in this field and seeing how easy it is
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对我来说，作为一名在这个领域工作的人，看到人们有多么容易

sentences.en: for people to come to believe and remember things that didn't happen,
sentences.zh: 去相信并记住那些从未发生过的事情，

sentences.en: when you see someone make a mistake in their memory, when somebody disagrees with you,
sentences.zh: 当你看到有人在记忆中犯错时，当有人与你意见不合，

sentences.en: and you're pretty convinced your memory is right,
sentences.zh: 而你相当确信自己的记忆是正确的，

sentences.en: at least you don't have to decide that your fellow human is a big, fat liar.
sentences.zh: 至少你不必认定你的同胞是个彻头彻尾的大骗子。

sentences.en: You can appreciate the fact that they just might have a false memory and they're human.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解这样一个事实：他们可能只是有了虚假记忆，他们也是人。

sentences.en: And I think that is a much kinder way to feel about our family members, our friends,
sentences.zh: 我认为，对于我们的家人、朋友，

sentences.en: our acquaintances, our others who say something that we don't agree with.
sentences.zh: 我们的熟人，以及那些说出我们不同意的话的其他人，这是一种更善良的心态。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Loftus is a psychologist at the University of California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·洛夫图斯是加州大学欧文分校的心理学家。

sentences.en: She's the author of The Myth of Repressed Memory and Witness for the Defense,
sentences.zh: 她是《压抑记忆的神话》和《为辩护人作证》的作者，

sentences.en: the accused, the eyewitness, and the expert who puts memory on trial.
sentences.zh: 她是涉案被告、目击证人，也是将记忆推上法庭的专家。
